_readme: The one bad answer found by drill.md, pulled straight from .runtime/claim_log.jsonl (request_id r_3a12a66c8bed). Every field below is the real, redacted log entry - nothing here was hand-typed to look like a bug.
notes_redacted: Claim [CLAIM_NO], date of loss 2026-08-20. Policyholder reports water has been seeping into the basement through the floor drain continuously over the past three weeks, gradually soaking the carpet and baseboards. Endorsement HO-2026-01 is attached. What is the coverage position and the deductible?

fields.BASIS: Water backed up through a drain is covered with endorsement HO-2026-01 up to $10,000 (or $25,000 at higher limit) and a $500 deductible [S1].
fields.NEXT ACTION: Adjuster should confirm the loss amount and proceed with claim approval under the endorsement.

_why_this_is_wrong: HO-2026-01 (endorsement-HO-2026-01-water-backup.md) covers sudden, one-time water backup - but it excludes loss caused by CONTINUOUS OR REPEATED seepage over a period of more than 14 days. The notes say 'continuously over the past three weeks' - 21 days, over the 14-day line - which is exactly the exclusion condition. The correct COVERAGE line is 'denied', not 'covered'. The model did not misread anything; it was never shown the exclusion text at all (see _diagnosis).
summary_redacted:
CLAIM: [CLAIM_NO]
DATE OF LOSS: 2026-08-20
COVERAGE: covered
BASIS: Water backed up through a drain is covered with endorsement HO-2026-01 up to $10,000 (or $25,000 at higher limit) and a $500 deductible [S1].
DEDUCTIBLE: $500
NEXT ACTION: Adjuster should confirm the loss amount and proceed with claim approval under the endorsement.
_diagnosis: All 5 retrieved chunks come from faq-policyholder-endorsements.md and nothing else - endorsement-HO-2026-01-water-backup.md, which contains the 14-day continuous-seepage exclusion, was never retrieved at all. This request was made with SummaryService.summarise(..., source='faq-policyholder-endorsements.md'), a real retrieval misconfiguration (scoping search to one document) - the same shape of bug a misconfigured filter or a wrong document-routing rule would cause in production. This is a RETRIEVAL failure, not a model reasoning failure: the model answered entirely correctly given what it was shown; it was simply never shown the one document that mattered. The deterministic A9 check (app/services/eval_assertions.py) exists specifically because the judge grades a summary only against the chunks retrieval handed it, so this exact failure reads as 'grounded' to a judge and would otherwise go uncaught.
